Assess re-identification risk

Source: R/deidentify.R
assess_reidentification_risk.Rd

Computes k-anonymity over a set of quasi-identifiers: for each record, how many other records share its combination of values. Records in small groups are the ones a person with background knowledge could single out.

assess_reidentification_risk(x, quasi_identifiers = NULL, k = 5L)

Arguments

x

A vcs_data object, or a data frame.

quasi_identifiers

Columns to treat as quasi-identifiers. Defaults to the geographic, demographic and design variables usually released.

k

Threshold below which a group is considered risky.

Value

A list of class vcs_risk with the k-anonymity distribution, the risky groups, and the proportion of records below k.

Details

This is a screening tool. It measures only what the chosen quasi-identifiers capture, and says nothing about identifiers hiding in free text.

See also

generalize_geography(), generalize_age()

Examples

r <- assess_reidentification_risk(vcs_example)
r
#> <vcs_risk: k-anonymity screening>
#>   quasi-identifiers: province, district, health_zone, health_area, residence, stratum, sex
#>   records          : 256
#>   minimum k        : 1
#>   median k         : 5
#>   unique records   : 6 (2.3%)
#>   below k = 5      : 90 (35.2%)
#>   Consider generalize_geography() or generalize_age() before release.
# Coarsening geography raises k.
coarse <- generalize_geography(vcs_example, lowest_level = "province")
assess_reidentification_risk(coarse)$prop_below_k
#> [1] 0
